titre: The Terracotta Army of Xi'an, Discovered by Farmers (1974)
accroche: In March 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an uncover the fragments of an army buried for 2,200 years.
contenu_vulgarise:
In March 1974, in Lintong County near Xi'an, six brothers of the Yang family and their neighbor Wang Puzhi dig a well about 1.5 kilometers east of the first emperor's burial mound, on land that has gone barren. Their shovel turns up fragments of figurines, and they alert the authorities. What archaeologists uncover in the following months is an army buried for more than 2,000 years to guard the tomb of China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang: to date, more than 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots, and several hundred horses, spread across four pits, one of which remains empty.

## Standardized production, 2,000 years before the assembly line

The most striking thing is not the number, it is the method. The imperial workshops did not sculpt each soldier from start to finish: they made heads, arms, legs, and torsos separately from a limited number of molds, then assembled these pieces before customizing each face by hand, mustache, hairstyle, expression. The result gives the illusion of 8,000 unique individuals, whereas production rests on interchangeable components. Another trace of this organization: sculptors signed their work under the figurines' armpits, and workshops marked the everyday objects they also produced with their name, a practice that today lets historians identify which workshops were put to work, among a workforce that mixed state laborers and local craftsmen.

## What the public has never seen

The soldiers visitors see today are a uniform gray, and that is an optical illusion of history: they came out of the ground painted in bright colors (cinnabar red, malachite green, azurite blue, charcoal black) fixed by a lacquer-based varnish. This varnish cannot withstand the air for long once a figurine is excavated: it can crack within 15 seconds of excavation and flake off within four minutes, taking the color with it. In other words, a good part of what the excavators of 1974 and the following years saw in color disappeared before it could be fixed in place. The imperial tomb itself remains unopened today, probably out of concern for preserving what it holds: the rapid degradation of color observed on the soldiers gives a sense of what would be at stake.

repere.texte: The varnish that protected the soldiers' original paint can crack within 15 seconds of excavation, and flake off within four minutes: the original cinnabar red, malachite green, and azurite blue have thus disappeared from many of the figures before they could be fixed in place.

carte.punch: More than 8,000 soldiers that all seem unique, assembled from standardized parts.
carte.idee: In 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an discover Emperor Qin's terracotta army: more than 8,000 soldiers, assembled from standardized parts and then customized face by face. Originally painted, they lose their color within minutes in the open air.

quiz.question: How did Emperor Qin's workshops produce 8,000 soldiers that are all different?
choix: By sculpting each soldier by hand, with no interchangeable parts
By assembling standardized parts, then sculpting a distinct face for each one
By casting all the soldiers in a single mold, reused 8,000 times
By hiring 8,000 sculptors, one per soldier, with no common step
quiz.explication: The workshops produced heads, arms, legs, and torsos separately before assembly, then a sculptor customized each face by hand and signed their work under the figurine's armpit, hence faces that are all different on standardized bodies, and not an individual sculpture or a single mold.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who discovered the Terracotta Army of Xi'an, and under what circumstances?
choix: Archaeologists carrying out a planned excavation in the Xi'an region
Railroad workers laying track near Lintong
Chinese soldiers on military maneuvers in Lintong County
Farmers digging a well on land that had gone barren
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Six brothers of the Yang family and their neighbor Wang Puzhi were digging a well on barren land in March 1974 when their shovel turned up fragments of figurines, which led to the discovery.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why have the soldiers' original colors almost all disappeared?
choix: Because archaeologists sandblasted them clean before display
Because the original clay held no pigment
Because the protective varnish cracks and flakes off within minutes in the open air
Because the farmers repainted the statues before alerting the authorities
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The lacquer-based varnish that fixed the colors can crack within 15 seconds of excavation and flake off within four minutes, taking the color with it.
